title: Engineering next-generation  Aspergillus  cell factories: advances in genetic engineering, synthetic biology, and metabolic reprogramming strategies
content: The filamentous fungal genus Aspergillus is one of the most prominent platforms in industrial biotechnology. Several members of this genus are widely recognised as efficient cell factories producing a wide range of high-value products, including enzymes, organic acids, and secondary metabolites. Despite their enormous industrial significance, conventional Aspergillus cell factories are often constrained by limited stress tolerance, sensitivity to fermentation inhibitors, metabolic bottlenecks, and bioprocess-associated challenges including mass, heat, and oxygen transfer limitations, which hinder the realisation of their full biotechnological potential. Recent advances in genetic engineering, coupled with growing knowledge of fungal genomics, have enabled the development of improved cell factories to meet ever-increasing industrial demands. In light of this, this review provides an overview of the current biotechnological potential of Aspergillus spp. and details recent technological advances that facilitate the development of genetically improved Aspergillus strains. It discusses various transformation methods, promoters, selectable markers, genome-editing technologies, metabolic engineering strategies, and advanced synthetic biology platforms, highlighting their strengths and limitations. In addition, the review highlights major systemic bottlenecks associated with Aspergillus spp. and the emerging opportunities offered by systems biology and artificial intelligence for predictive strain engineering. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on technological advances, challenges, and emerging opportunities in Aspergillus engineering, establishing an integrated framework for developing next-generation cell factories.
